translations.text: And God called Moses, and the Lord spoke to him from the tent of witness:
Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them: If any man among you offers an offering as a sacrifice to God, offer your sacrifice from the livestock, from the cattle and from the sheep.
If his sacrifice is a whole burnt offering, he shall bring a male calf without blemish from the cattle to the doors of the tent of witness, and he shall offer it as acceptable before the Lord.
And he shall lay his hand on the head of the offering, so that it may be acceptable for him and make atonement for him.
And they shall slaughter the calf before the Lord, and the sons of Aaron, the priests, shall offer its blood and sprinkle its blood around the altar that is at the doors of the tent of witness.
And they shall flay the whole offering and divide it limb by limb.
And the sons of Aaron, the priests, shall put fire on the altar and heap wood on the fire.
And the sons of Aaron, the priests, shall arrange the cut pieces, the head and the fat, on the wood and on the fire that is on the altar.
But you shall wash the entrails and the feet with water, and the priest shall arrange all of this on the altar. This is a fruit-offering, an offering, an odor of fragrance to the Lord.
If his offering to God is from the flock, from the lambs or from the kids, he shall bring a ram without blemish as a whole burnt offering, and they shall lay his hand on its head.
And they shall slaughter it at the side of the altar, on the north side, before the Lord, and the sons of Aaron, the priests, shall sprinkle its blood around the altar.
And they shall divide it limb by limb, and the priests shall arrange the head and the fat on the wood
But its entrails and its feet shall be washed with water. The priest shall offer all of this and place it on the altar. It is a fruit-offering, an offering, an odor of fragrance to the Lord.
If he offers a fruit-offering from the birds as a sacrifice to God, and offers his offering from the turtledoves or from the young of the pigeons,
then the priest shall bring it to the altar, and the priest shall cut off its head and place it on the altar, and he shall drain its blood at the base of the altar.
And he shall cut away what is stuck [?] together with the feathers, and cast them out from the altar toward the east, to the place of the sacrifice.
And he shall break it at the wings but not divide it, and the priest shall place it on the altar, on the wood and on the fire. It is a fruit-offering, an offering, as an odor of fragrance to God.
If a soul offers a gift as an offering to God, his offering shall be fine flour, and he shall pour oil on it and put frankincense on it. This is an offering.

And he shall bring it to the sons of Aaron, the priests, and the priest shall take from it a full handful of the fine flour with the oil, and all its frankincense. And the priest shall place it on the altar as an odor of fragrance to God.
And the rest of the sacrifice shall belong to Aaron and his sons, as something holy among the sacrifices of God.
And if he offers a gift as an offering baked in an oven, it shall be of fine flour: unleavened loaves mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers anointed with oil.
If your gift is an offering from the griddle, it shall be fine flour mixed with oil, unleavened.
And you shall break it into crumbled pieces and pour oil on it. It is an offering to God.
If your gift is an offering from the griddle, it shall be made of fine flour with oil.
And he shall offer to God the sacrifice that is made from one of these. He shall bring it to the priest, and the priest shall approach the altar
and take from the sacrifice its memorial portion, and the priest shall lay it on the altar as a fruit-offering, for a fragrant savour to God.
And the remainder of the offering shall belong to Aaron and his sons, most holy among the fruit-offerings of God.
Every offering that you offer to God you shall not make with leaven, for you shall not offer any leaven or any honey as a fruit-offering to God.
And as a gift, as a first offering to God, but it shall not go up on the altar for a fragrant savour to God.
And every offering of your sacrifice shall be salted with salt. You shall not leave the salt of the law of God out of your offerings, and you shall put salt on every offering of yours.
If you offer to God an offering of first fruits, new, roasted, fresh, crushed grain to God, you shall offer it as a sacrifice of first fruits,
and you shall pour oil on it and put frankincense on it: this is an offering.
And the priest shall offer its memorial portion from the groats together with the oil, and all its frankincense: this is an offering to God.
If his sacrifice to God is an offering of life, if he offers it from the cattle, whether a male or a female, he shall bring it unblemished before God.

And he shall lay his hands on the head of the offering, and they shall slaughter it at the doors of the tent of witness, and the sons of Aaron, the priests, shall pour out its blood around the altar of whole burnt offerings.
And from the offering of life they shall take, as a fruit-offering to God, the fat that covers the entrails and all the fat of the belly,
and the two kidneys and the fat that is on them; he shall cut it off together with the kidneys.
And the sons of Aaron, the priests, shall offer them on the altar of offerings, on the wood and the fire, as a fruit-offering, a fragrant savour to God.
If his sacrifice to God for his offering of life is from the flock, male or female, he shall bring it unblemished.
If he brings a lamb as his offering, he shall bring it before God.
And he shall lay his hands on the head of his offering and slaughter it at the doors of the tent of witness, and the sons of Aaron, the priests, shall pour out its blood around the altar.

And he shall offer the offering of life as a sacrifice to God: the fat and the unblemished loins; he shall cut it off together with the thigh, and the fat that covers the entrails and all the fat of the belly,
and the two kidneys and the fat on them, which is on the thighs, and he shall remove the lobes of the liver together with the kidneys.
And the priest shall offer it on the altar for a fragrant savour, a sacrifice to God.
Or if his offering is from the goats, he shall bring it before God.
And he shall lay his hands on it, and they shall slaughter it before God at the doors of the tent of witness, and the sons of Aaron, the priests, shall pour out its blood around the altar.
And from it he shall offer as a sacrifice to God the fat that covers the entrails and all the fat of the belly.
And he shall cut off the two kidneys and the fat that is on them, which is by the thighs, and the lobes of the liver together with the kidneys.
And the priest shall offer it on the altar as an offering, as a sweet savour to God; all the fat is God's.
It is an everlasting statute throughout your generations: you shall not eat any fat or any blood.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
Speak to the sons of Israel and say: If a person sins before God unintentionally against any of God's commandments about things that ought not to be done, and does any one of them,
if the anointed chief priest sins so as to bring sin on the people, then for the sin that he has committed he shall bring a calf from the cattle, without blemish, before God for his sin.
And he shall bring it to the door of the tent of witness before God, and lay his hand on the head of the calf before God, and slaughter the calf before God.
And the anointed priest, who has been consecrated, shall take some of the calf's blood in his hand and bring it into the tent of witness.
And the priest shall dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle some of the blood seven times with his finger before God, by the holy veil.

And he shall smear some of the calf's blood on the horns of the altar of compounded incense before God, which is in the tent of witness. And he shall pour out all the rest of the calf's blood at the base of the altar of offerings, which is before the doors of the tent of witness.
And he shall remove all the fat from the calf of the sin offering: the fat [?] of the entrails,
and the two kidneys and the fat on them, which is by the thighs, and the base of the liver together with the kidneys he shall remove,
just as they remove them from the calf of the peace offering. And the priest shall offer them on the altar of offerings.
And the skin of the calf and all its flesh, with its head and feet, its entrails and its dung,

in short, the whole calf he shall carry out of the camp to a clean place, where the ashes are poured out. There they shall burn it on wood with fire at the place where the ashes are poured out, and it shall be burned up.

If the whole congregation of the sons of Israel errs through ignorance, unintentionally, and the matter is hidden from the eyes of the congregation, and they do any one of God's commandments about things that ought not to be done,
and the sin that they have committed becomes known, the congregation shall bring a calf from the cattle, without blemish, for the sin, and they shall bring it to the doors of the tent of witness.
And the elders of the people shall lay their hands on the head of the calf before God.
And the anointed priest shall bring some of the calf's blood into the tent of witness.
And the priest shall dip his finger in the calf's blood and sprinkle it seven times before God, facing the veil of the sanctuary.

And he shall smear some of that same blood on the horns of the altar of incense that stands before God, which is in the tent of witness. And he shall pour out all the rest of the blood at the base of the altar of offerings, which is at the doors of the tent of witness.
And he shall remove all the fat from it and offer it on the altar.

And he shall do with this calf just as he did with the calf of the sin offering; he shall do the same with this one. And the priest shall make atonement for them, and their sins shall be forgiven them.
And they shall carry the calf outside the camp and burn it, just as they burned the first calf. This is for the sin of the congregation.
If a ruler sins and unintentionally does any one of all the commandments of the Lord his God that ought not to be done, and so sins,
and the sin he committed becomes known, he shall bring as his offering a kid of the goats, an unblemished male goat,
and he shall lay his hand on the head of the goat, and they shall slaughter it in the place before God where they slaughter the whole burnt offerings.

And the priest shall take some of the blood of the sin offering and smear it with his finger on the horns of the altar of whole burnt offerings, and he shall pour out all its blood against the side of the altar of whole burnt offerings.
And he shall offer all its fat on the altar, like the fat of the sacrifice of salvation. And the priest shall make atonement for him for his sin, and it shall be forgiven him.
If any one person of the people of the land sins unintentionally and does any one of the commandments of God that ought not to be done, and so does it,
and the sin he committed becomes known, he shall bring a kid of the goats, an unblemished female, for the sin he committed,
and he shall lay his hand on the head of the one that is for sin, and they shall slaughter the kid of the sin offering in the place where they slaughter the whole burnt offerings.
And the priest shall take some of its blood with his finger and smear it on the horns of the altar of whole burnt offerings, and he shall pour out all its blood at the base of the altar.

And he shall remove all its fat, just as the fat is removed from the offering, and the priest shall offer it on the altar as a sweet savour to God. And the priest shall make atonement for him, and it shall be forgiven him.
If he offers a sheep as a sacrifice for his sin, he shall offer an unblemished female.
And he shall lay his hand on the head of the sin offering, and they shall slaughter it in the place where they slaughter the whole burnt offerings.

And the priest shall take some of the blood of the sin offering with his finger and smear it on the horns of the altar of whole burnt offerings, and he shall pour out all of its blood at the base of the altar.

And he shall remove all its fat, just as the fat is removed from the sheep of the offering of salvation, and the priest shall smear it on the altar of sacrifices before God. And the priest shall make atonement for his sin, and it shall be forgiven him.
If a person sins in this way: he hears the voice of an oath, and he is a witness, whether he saw it or knows of it, and he does not tell, then he has taken his sin upon himself.
A person who touches any unclean thing, whether a carcass, or an unclean animal torn by wild beasts, or the dead body of any abominable unclean creature,
or who touches some uncleanness of a human being, any uncleanness of his that he touches and becomes defiled by, and he forgot it, and afterwards he learns of it and has sinned;

and a person who swears and declares with his own mouth that he will do evil or do good, in anything at all that a person promises by oath, and he forgot it, and then he learns of it and has sinned in any one of these,
And he shall declare to him the sin that he has committed.

And for what he has sinned he shall offer to God a female from the flock, a lamb, or a kid from the goats, as a sin offering. And the priest shall make atonement for that sin, and the sin shall be forgiven him.
If he cannot afford a sheep, then for the sin he has committed he shall offer to God two turtledoves or two young pigeons: one as a sin offering and one as a whole burnt offering.
And he shall bring them to the priest, and the priest shall offer the one for the sin offering first. The priest shall wring its head off at the neck [?], but shall not divide it in two.
And he shall sprinkle some of the blood of the sin offering on the wall of the altar, and the rest of the blood he shall drain out at the base of the altar, for it is a sin offering.
And the second he shall make a whole burnt offering, as is required. And the priest shall make atonement for him for the sin he has committed, and it shall be forgiven him.

If he cannot find a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons, then as his offering for his sin he shall bring a tenth of a measure of fine flour as a sin offering. He shall not pour oil on it or put frankincense on it, for it is a sin offering.
And he shall bring it to the priest, and the priest shall take a full handful of it as its memorial portion and lay it on the altar of sacrifices before God. It is a sin offering.

And the priest shall make atonement for him for the sin he committed in any one of these things, whichever he could find and offered, and it shall be forgiven him. The remainder shall belong to the priest, like a sacrifice of praise.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:

If a person forgets something through forgetfulness and sins unintentionally in regard to the holy things of God, then for his sin he shall offer to God an unblemished ram from the flock, valued in silver by weight, by the holy shekel, for the thing in which he became guilty.

And because he has sinned in regard to his holy things, he shall pay it back and add a fifth to it, and give it to the priest. And the priest shall make atonement for him with the ram of the guilt offering, and it shall be forgiven him.
And if a person sins and does any one of the things forbidden by the commandments of God, which ought not to be done, and did not realize it, and became guilty and incurred the sin,

he shall bring to the priest an unblemished ram from the flock, valued in silver, for his guilt. And the priest shall make atonement for his ignorance, in which he did not realize it and did not know, and it shall be forgiven him,
for he has committed a sin before God.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:
If a person sins and heedlessly disregards the commandments of the Lord, and lies to his neighbor about a deposit, or about a partnership, or about robbery, or wrongs his neighbor in any way,
or if he has found something lost and lied about it, and sworn falsely about any one of these things that a person does and sins by them,
then when he has sinned and become guilty, he shall give back what he took by robbery, or make good the harm he did, or return the deposit that was entrusted to him, or the lost thing that he found,
or anything about which he swore falsely. He shall pay back the principal itself and add a fifth to it. He shall give it to the person to whom it belongs, on the day he is convicted.
And for his guilt he shall offer to God an unblemished ram, at the value of the thing in which he became guilty.
And the priest shall make atonement for him before God, and he shall be forgiven for any one of the things that he did in sin.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said:

Command Aaron and his sons and say: This is the law of the whole burnt offerings. This whole burnt offering shall stay on its burning place on the altar all night until morning, and the fire of the altar shall burn on it and shall not be put out.

And the priest shall put on the linen garment, and he shall put breeches on his body. He shall take up from the altar the offering that the fire has consumed, the whole burnt offering, and lay it beside the altar.
And he shall take off his garment and put on another, and he shall carry what was offered as an offering out of the camp to a holy place.

And the fire shall burn on the altar and shall not be put out. The priest shall kindle wood on it every morning, and lay the whole burnt offering out on it, and place on it the fat of the peace offering.
And the fire shall burn on the altar continually and shall not be put out.
This is the law of the offerings that the sons of Aaron shall bring before God, in front of the altar.

And he shall take from the altar a handful of the fine flour, with its oil and with its frankincense that is on the offering, and he shall offer it on the altar as an offering, as a sweet savour, its memorial portion to the Lord God.
And Aaron and his sons shall eat the rest of it. It shall be eaten unleavened in a holy place, in the court of the tent of witness, where they shall eat it.
It shall not be baked with leaven. I have given it to them as a portion of the offerings of God. It is most holy, like the sin offering and like the trespass offering.
Every male of the priests shall eat it, as an everlasting ordinance throughout your generations, from the offerings of God. Everyone who touches it shall be made holy.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said:

This is the offering of Aaron and his sons, which they shall offer to God on the day on which he anoints them: a tenth of a measure of fine flour as a perpetual sacrifice, half of it in the morning and half of it in the evening.
It shall be made on a griddle, mixed with oil. He shall offer it twisted, a sacrifice of broken pieces, an offering, as a sweet savour to God.
The priest from among his sons who is anointed in his place shall do it. It is an everlasting ordinance; it shall be wholly burned on the altar.
And every sacrifice of a priest shall be wholly burned and shall not be eaten.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said:

Speak to Aaron and his sons and say: This is the law of the sin offering. In the place where they slaughter the whole burnt offerings, they shall slaughter the sin offering before God. It is most holy.
The priest who offers it shall eat it himself. He shall eat it in a holy place, in the court of the tent of witness.
Everyone who touches its flesh shall be made holy. If some of its blood is sprinkled on someone's garment and stains it, he shall wash it in a holy place.
And the earthenware vessel in which it is boiled shall be broken. If it is boiled in a bronze vessel, he shall scour it and rinse it with water.
Every male of the priests shall eat it. It is most holy to God.
But no sin offering whose blood is brought into the tent of witness to make atonement in the sanctuary shall be eaten. It shall be burned with fire.
And this is the law of the ram that is for sin, for it is most holy.
In the place where they slaughter the whole burnt offerings, they shall also slaughter the ram for sin before God, and they shall sprinkle its blood around the altar.
And he shall take its fat from it: the fat of the belly, and all the fat that covers the inner parts, and all the fat that is on the entrails.
And he shall remove the two kidneys and the fat on them, which is on the thighs, and the lobe of the liver together with the kidneys.
And the priest shall offer them on the altar as a fruit-offering, a sweet savour to God, for it is for sin.
Every male among the priests shall eat it; they shall eat it in a holy place, for it is most holy.
As with the offering for sin, so with the offering for guilt: there is one law for them. It belongs to the priest; whoever makes atonement, it shall be his.
The priest who offers a man's sacrifice shall also have the skin of the whole burnt offering that he offers.
And every offering that is made in the oven, and everything that is made in the pan or on the griddle, shall belong to the priest who offers it.
For every offering, whether made with oil or made without oil, shall belong to all the sons of Aaron, to each one equally.
This is the law of the sacrifice of salvation that one offers to God.
If he offers it for praise, then along with the sacrifice of praise he shall offer loaves of fine flour smeared with oil, and fine flour worked up with oil.
With loaves of leavened bread he shall offer his offering along with the sacrifice of praise.

And from all of this offering of his he shall bring one of each as a first-fruit offering to the Lord God. It shall belong to the priest who sprinkles the blood of the sacrifice of salvation, and the sacrifice too.
And the flesh of the sacrifice of praise of salvation shall be his as well. On the day he offers it he shall eat it; he shall not leave any of it until morning.
And if he offers his sacrifice in fulfilment of a vow or as a freewill offering, they shall eat it on the day he offers his sacrifice, and also on the next day.
Whatever is left of the offering until the third day shall be burned with fire.
If he does eat any of its flesh on the third day, it is not accepted, for it is a defilement. And the person who eats any of it shall bring sin upon his own head.
And flesh that touches anything unclean shall not be eaten; let it be burned with fire. Everyone who is clean may eat the flesh.
But the person who eats of the flesh of the sacrifice of salvation, which is God's, while his uncleanness is upon him, that soul shall perish from among his people.

And a person who touches an unclean thing, whether human uncleanness, or unclean four-footed animals, or any unclean abomination, and eats of the flesh of the sacrifice of salvation, which is the Lord's, that person shall perish from among his people.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
Speak to the children of Israel and say to them: You shall not eat any fat of cattle, sheep or goats.
And the fat of an animal that has died and of one torn by wild beasts may be used for any work, but it shall certainly not be eaten.
Anyone who eats the fat of the animals that you offer as a sacrifice to God, that person who eats it shall perish from among his people.
You shall not eat any of this blood in any of your dwellings, whether of birds or of cattle.
Every person who eats blood, that soul shall be destroyed from among his people.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
Speak to the sons of Israel and say: Whoever offers a sacrifice of peace offering to God shall bring his offering to God from the sacrifice of peace offering;
with his own hands he shall bring his offering to God: this is the fat of the breast and the lobe of the liver. He shall bring it so as to set it as a set offering before God.
And the priest shall offer the fat on the altar, and the breast shall belong to Aaron and his sons.
And the right shoulder you shall give to the priest as an offering from the offerings of your peace offerings.
Whoever of the sons of Aaron offers the blood of the peace offering and the fat, the right shoulder shall be his as a portion,

for the breast of the set offering and the shoulder of the offering I have taken from the sons of Israel, from the sacrifices of your peace offerings, and I have given them to Aaron and his sons as a perpetual ordinance from the sons of Israel.
This is the anointing of Aaron and the anointing of his sons from the offerings of God, on the day on which he brought them forward to serve as priests of God,
as God commanded that it be given to them on the day on which he anointed them, from the sons of Israel, as a perpetual ordinance among their generations.
This is the law of the whole burnt offerings and of the offerings, and of those that are for sins and for trespass, for consecration, and for the sacrifices of peace offerings,
as God commanded Moses on Mount Sinai on the day on which he ordered the sons of Israel to offer their sacrifices before God in the wilderness of Sinai.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
Bring Aaron and his sons, and their garments, and the oil of anointing, and the calf for sin, and the two rams, and the basket of unleavened bread.
And gather all the people at the door of the tent of witness.
And Moses did as God had commanded him, and he called the whole congregation of the people to the door of the tent of witness.
And Moses said to the congregation: This is the word which God has commanded me to do.
And Moses brought Aaron and his sons and washed them with water.

And he clothed them with the garments, and girded them with the girdles, and put the shoes on them, and put the shoulder-piece upon them, and girded it according to its workmanship and fastened it with it.
And he put the oracle-piece upon the shoulder-pieces, and on the oracle-piece he placed the Manifestation and the Truth.
And he wrapped the mitre around his head, and on the mitre, at the very front, he placed the gold plate, the purified holy thing, as God had commanded Moses.
And Moses took some of the anointing oil

and sprinkled it on them and on the altar seven times [?: "10 Ⴁ", apparently an intrusive marginal or folio mark], and anointed the altar and consecrated it, and all its vessels, and the laver and its stand, and consecrated it. And he anointed the tent and everything that was in it, and consecrated it.
And Moses poured some of the anointing oil on Aaron's head, anointed him and consecrated him.
Moses brought the sons of Aaron, clothed them in garments, girded them with sashes and put caps on their heads, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
And he brought forward the young bull for the sin offering, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the head of the young bull of the sin offering.

And he slaughtered it, and Moses took some of its blood and with his own finger smeared it on the horns of the altar all around, and he purified the altar. He poured out the blood at the base of the altar and consecrated it, so that atonement could be made on it.
And he took all the fat of the entrails, the lobe of the liver, the two kidneys and the fat on them, and Moses offered them on the altar.
They burned the young bull, its hide, all its flesh and its dung with fire outside the camp, as God had commanded Moses.
And Moses brought forward the ram for the whole burnt offering, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the head of the ram.
And Moses slaughtered the ram and sprinkled its blood around the altar.
And he cut the ram into pieces, and Moses offered its head, its pieces and the fat.

He washed its entrails and its feet with water, and Moses offered the whole ram on the altar. It is a whole burnt offering, a pleasing fragrance; it is an offering made to God, as God had commanded Moses.
And Moses brought forward the second ram, the ram of consecration, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the head of the ram.
And he slaughtered it, and Moses took some of its blood and smeared it on the lobe of Aaron's right ear, on the tips of the fingers of his right hand and on the tips of the toes of his right foot.

And Moses brought Aaron's sons and smeared some of the blood on the lobes of their right ears, on the fingers of their right hands and on the toes of their right feet. And Moses sprinkled the blood around the altar.
And he took the fat of the belly, the fat of the tail, the lobe of the liver, the two kidneys and the fat on them, and the right shoulder.
And from the basket of consecration that was before God he took one unleavened loaf, one loaf made with oil and one wafer, and placed them on the fat and on the right shoulder.
And he put all of this in Aaron's hands and in the hands of his sons, and lifted it up as an offering before God.
And Moses took it from their hands and offered it on the altar on top of the whole burnt offerings of consecration, as a pleasing fragrance: this is a sacrifice to God.
And Moses took the breast and set it apart as an offering before God from the ram of consecration, and it became Moses' portion, as God had commanded Moses.

And Moses took some of the anointing oil and some of the blood from the altar, and sprinkled it on Aaron and his garments, and on his sons and their garments. And he consecrated Aaron and his garments, and his sons and their garments with him.

And Moses said to Aaron and his sons: "Boil that flesh in the court of the tent of witness, in a holy place, and eat it there, together with the loaves that are in the basket of consecration, as the Lord commanded me, saying: 'Aaron and his sons shall eat it.'"
"And burn with fire whatever is left of the flesh and the bread."
And do not go out from the door of the tent of witness for seven days, until the day when your consecration is completed, for in seven days your hands will be made perfect,
just as he has done on this day, which God commanded me to do, so that atonement may be made for you.
And you shall sit at the doors of the tent of witness for seven days and nights, and keep the charge of God, so that you do not perish, for this is what God commanded me.
And Aaron and his sons did all the things that God had commanded Moses.
And on the eighth day Moses called Aaron and his sons and the elders of Israel.
And Moses said to Aaron and his sons: Take for yourself a calf from the cattle for sin, and the ram for a whole burnt offering, unblemished, and offer them before God.
And speak to the elders of Israel and say: Take one he-goat from the goats for sin, and a ram, and a calf, and a yearling lamb as a sacrifice, all of them unblemished,
and a young bull and a ram as a salvation offering before God, and fine flour mixed with oil, for the Lord will appear among you.
And they brought them before the doors of the tent of witness, as Moses had commanded, and the whole congregation came and stood before God.
And Moses said to them: This is the thing that God has told you to do, and the glory of God will appear among you.

And Moses said to Aaron: Go up to the altar of God and offer your sin offering and your sacrifice, and make atonement for yourself and for your house. Then offer the sacrifice of the people and make atonement for them, as the Lord commanded me.
And Aaron went up to the altar and slaughtered the calf of the sin offering.
And the sons of Aaron brought the blood to him. And he dipped his finger in the blood and anointed the horns of the altar with it. And he poured out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar.
And he offered on the altar the fat and the kidneys and the lobe of the liver from the sin offering, as God had commanded Moses.
And they burned its flesh and hide and dung outside the camp.
And he slaughtered the whole burnt offering, and the priests, Aaron's sons, brought the blood to their father, and he sprinkled it around the altar.
And they brought him the whole burnt offering piece by piece, with its head, and he laid it on the altar.
And they washed its entrails and its feet with water, and he laid these too on the altar of whole burnt offerings.
And they brought the people's offering, and led in the he-goat for the people's sin, and he slaughtered it like the first.
And they brought the whole burnt offering, and he did the same with it, as was proper.
And they brought the offering, and his hands were filled from it, and he laid it on the altar, besides the morning sacrifice.
And he slaughtered the calf and the ram of the salvation offering for the people. And the sons of Aaron brought their blood to their father,
and the fat from the calf and from the ram: the belly, the fat covering the [?], all the fat of the entrails, the two kidneys with the fat on them, and the lobe of the liver.
And he placed the fat on the breast, and offered these fats on the altar.
And Aaron set apart the breast and the right shoulder to be lifted up as an offering before God, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
And Aaron lifted up his hands over the people and blessed them. He came down after he had offered the sacrifice, the one for sins and the one for peace.
And Moses and Aaron went into the tent of witness. When they came out from there, they blessed the people. And the glory of God appeared to all the people.

And fire came out from God and consumed everything that was on the altar, the whole burnt offering and the fat portions. All the people saw it and were amazed, and they fell on their faces and worshipped.
And the two sons of Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, each took his censer, put fire in it and poured incense on it, and they brought strange fire before God, which God had not commanded them.
And fire came out from God and burned them up, and they died before God.

And Moses said to Aaron: "This is what God spoke of when he said: 'Among those who come near me I will be made holy, and among the whole congregation I will be glorified.'" And Aaron was deeply grieved.
And Moses called Mishael and Elzaphan, the sons of Uzziel, sons of Aaron's father's brother, and said to them: "Come, take up your brothers from before the sanctuary and carry them outside the camp."
And they came out and took them up in their garments and carried them outside the camp, as Moses had commanded them.

And Moses said to Aaron and to Eleazar and Ithamar, the sons of Aaron who were left: "Do not take the headdress off your heads, and do not tear your garments, so that you do not die and wrath does not come upon the whole congregation. But your brothers, the whole house of Israel, shall weep for the burning by which they were burned by God.
And you shall not go out from the door of the tent of witness, for the anointing oil from God is upon you." And they did as Moses had commanded.
And the Lord spoke to Aaron and said:

"You and your sons shall not drink wine or strong drink when you go into the tent of witness or when you approach the altar, so that you do not die. This is an everlasting law throughout your generations,
so that you distinguish between the holy and the profane, and between the unclean and the worthy,
and so that you teach the children of Israel all the law that God spoke to them through Moses."

And Moses said to Aaron and to Eleazar and Ithamar, his remaining sons: "Take the offering that is left over from the offerings made to God, and eat it unleavened beside the altar, for it is most holy.
And you shall eat it in a holy place, for this is the law for you and the law for your sons, from the holy offerings of God, for so I have been commanded.

And the breast that is set apart and the shoulder of the offering you shall eat in a holy place, you and your sons and your household with you, for they have been given as a law for you and a law for your sons from the peace offerings of the children of Israel.

The shoulder of the offering and the breast that is set apart they shall bring together with the fat portions, as a portion set apart before God. And it shall belong to you and to your sons and your daughters with you as an everlasting law, as God commanded Moses."
And Moses searched diligently for the goat of the sin offering, and it had been burned up. And Moses was angry with Eleazar and Ithamar, the sons of Aaron who were left, and said to them:
Why did you not eat this sin offering in the holy place? For it is most holy, and he gave it to you to eat, so that you might take away the sins of the people and make atonement for them before God.
For none of its blood was brought into the sanctuary; you should have eaten it before [the Lord], face to face, in the holy place, as the Lord commanded me.

And Aaron spoke to Moses and said to him: If only today they have brought their sin offerings before God, and such things have befallen me, and I were to eat this sin offering today, would it not perhaps be displeasing to God?
And Moses heard this, and it pleased him.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and said to them:
Speak to the children of Israel and say to them: These are the animals that you may eat out of all the animals of the earth:
Every animal among the animals whose hoof is divided and is cleft into claws, and that brings up the cud, this you may eat.

But of these you shall not eat, those that bring up the cud and whose hoof is not divided, and those that are cleft into claws: the camel, for it brings up the cud but its hoof is not split; it is unclean to you;
and the hare, for it brings up the cud but its hoof is not split; it is unclean to you;
and the badger, for it brings up the cud but its hoof is not split; it is unclean to you;
and the pig, for its hoof is split and it is cleft into claws of the hoof, but it does not bring up the cud; it is unclean to you.
You shall not eat their flesh, and you shall not touch their carcasses, for these are unclean among you.
And these you may eat out of all that are in the waters: everything that has fins and scales in the waters, both in the sea and in the rivers, that you may eat;
and everything that does not have fins or scales in the waters, whether in the sea or in the rivers, which the waters bring forth, of every living creature that is in the waters, is abominable,
and let it be abominable to you: you shall not eat their flesh, and you shall loathe their carcasses.
And everything that has no fins and scales in the waters, this is abominable to you.
And these you shall loathe among the birds and shall not eat, for they are abominable: the vulture, and the heron, and the kite,
and the zarnasovi [?], the dzerkori [?], and its like;
the raven and its like;
and the seri [?], and the chahri [?], and its like; and the hawk and its like; the owl,
and the night-caller, and the sparrowhawk, and the dzendzeruki [?],
and the dedamtrvali [?], and the varkhvi [?], and the mghrinavi [?],
and the tivquavi [?], and the bukioti [?], and its like; and the hoopoe, and the bat,
and every winged creeping thing that goes on four
which have legs above their feet for leaping with them on the earth.
And these are the ones among them that you shall not eat: the fly and its kind, the wasp and its kind, the locust and its kind, the snake-fighter and its kind.
And every creeping thing among the winged creatures that has four feet is abominable to you, and you shall not defile yourselves with them.
Everyone who touches a dead one of them shall be unclean until evening,
and everyone who touches their carcass shall wash his garment and shall be unclean until evening.

Among all the cattle, any whose hoof is divided and cleft with a claw but which does not chew the cud shall be unclean to you. Everyone who touches the carcass of one of them shall be unclean until evening.
And everything that walks on its paws, among all the beasts that go on four feet, is unclean to you. Everyone who touches its carcass shall be unclean until evening.
And whoever picks up a dead one of them with his hand shall wash his garment and bathe in water, and he shall be unclean until evening, for all these are unclean to you.
And these also are unclean to you among the creeping things that creep on the earth: the weasel, the mouse, and the crocodile that lives on dry land,
and the shrew, the chameleon, the spotted lizard, the lizard, and the mole.
All these are unclean to you among all the creeping things that creep on the earth. Everyone who touches the carcass of one of them shall be unclean until evening.

Anything into which a dead one of these falls shall be unclean: any wooden vessel, or garment, or skin, or sackcloth. Every vessel used for any work shall be washed with water and shall be unclean until evening, and then it shall be clean.
And if one of them falls into any earthenware vessel, whatever is inside it is unclean, and the vessel shall be broken.
And any food that is eaten which water has come upon shall be unclean, and any drink that is drunk from any such vessel is unclean.
And anything on which a dead one of them falls shall be unclean. Ovens and pot-stands shall be broken down, for they are unclean, and they shall be unclean to you,
except for springs of water, a cistern, and a pool where water collects. All these are clean, but whoever touches their dead shall be unclean.
If one of their carcasses falls on any seed for sowing that is to be sown, it shall be clean.
If water is poured on any seed and a carcass of one of them falls on it, it shall be unclean to you.
If one of the cattle that is [?] for food dies, whoever touches its carcass shall be unclean until evening.

And whoever eats a dead one of them shall wash his garment and shall be unclean until evening. And whoever picks up the carcass of one of these shall wash his garment and shall be unclean until evening.
And every creeping thing that creeps on the face of the earth is abominable to you. It shall not be eaten.

Everything that goes on its belly, and everything that always goes on four feet, and whatever has many feet among all the creeping things that are on the earth, you shall not eat, for it is abominable.
And do not make your souls abominable with any of these creeping things that creep upon the earth; do not defile yourselves with them, and do not be unclean through them.
For I am the Lord your God; sanctify yourselves and be holy, for I, your Lord, am holy. And do not let your souls be defiled by any of the creeping things that move upon the earth.
For I am your God, who brought you out [?]
